injuries.name: Eeli Tolvanen
injuries.note: Tolvanen has appeared in each of the Rangers' first 12 games of the regular season, but his status for Saturday's matchup against Ottawa appears to be in question following his absence from practice. He's recorded three goals, an assist, 18 hits, 12 blocked shots and four PIM while averaging 13:01 of ice time to begin the year. Matt Rempe and Luke Glendening will be candidates to enter the lineup against the Senators if Tolvanen is unavailable.

injuries.name: Igor Shesterkin
injuries.note: Shesterkin was hurt during Friday's game against the Capitals when his right leg got jammed into the post while returning to the crease on a scrambled play, and the Rangers ruled him out for the season a day later. He was placed on injured reserve Sunday, and the team has now provided some clarification on the exact nature of his injury. Dylan Garand is slated to serve as the Rangers' No. 1 option in the crease until Joonas Korpisalo (lower body) is back in action.

injuries.name: Joe Veleno
injuries.note: Veleno has already missed the last two games, and he is slated to miss at least three more months. He hasn't earned a point in four appearances this season, but he has contributed two shots on goal, five blocked shots and seven hits.

injuries.name: Joonas Korpisalo
injuries.note: Korpisalo has already missed the first six games of the season and remains on injured reserve. The Rangers announced Saturday that Igor Shesterkin (lower body) will miss the remainder of the 2026-27 campaign. With Korpisalo and Shesterkin unavailable, Dylan Garand is currently the Rangers' No. 1 goaltender.

injuries.name: Nick Blankenburg
injuries.note: Blankenburg exited Thursday's matchup against the Rangers due to an undisclosed injury, and while the exact nature and severity haven't yet been revealed, he'll be forced to miss at least a week. Marshall Rifai (lower body) was also placed on injured reserve Friday, so Dakota Mermis and Cole McWard were called up to provide additional depth on the Maple Leafs' blue line.

injuries.name: Dakota Joshua
injuries.note: Joshua hasn't played this season yet because of a core muscle injury. He practiced with the Marlies on Friday, according to Joshua Kloke of The Athletic, but it's unclear when the 30-year-old forward will be available to play in the minors. Joshua had 10 goals, 18 points, 49 PIM and 195 hits in 55 NHL regular-season appearances for the Maple Leafs in 2025-26.

injuries.name: Miles Wood
injuries.note: ir

injuries.name: Chris Tanev
injuries.note: Tanev landed on injured reserve Sunday after he suffered an upper-body injury against Colorado on Saturday. Thursday's update indicates that he'll likely need to spend more than the minimum amount of time on injured reserve before he's in the mix to return to game action. Nick Blankenburg will likely continue to see time in Toronto's lineup while Tanev is sidelined.

injuries.name: Max Domi
injuries.note: There's no timetable for Domi's return after he had complications while undergoing surgery over the summer. The 31-year-old had 12 goals, 36 points and 95 PIM in 80 regular-season appearances with Toronto in 2025-26. Domi will likely serve in a middle-six capacity once he's ready to return.

injuries.name: Cade Webber
injuries.note: ir-nr

injuries.name: Elvis Merzlikins
injuries.note: Less than 24 hours after Merzlikins was traded to the Maple Leafs, a timetable for his return to action has been provided. The 32-year-old backstop had an up and down season in 2025-26, where he posted a 14-11-3 record, a 3.39 GAA and an .883 save percentage across 30 regular-season outings. He won't be rushed into action, as the Leafs new goaltender tandem of Sergei Bobrovsky and Anthony Stolarz are still expected to handle the majority of reps between the pipes this upcoming season. However, when Merzlikins is ready to return, he's the clear No. 3 option in Toronto's organization and could still see some playing time at the NHL level if he isn't sent down to AHL Toronto.
